sentences.text: 2) The brief material facts relevant for disposal of this criminal revision petition are that complainant Ms. Kavita Sharma lodged a complaint against the accused persons vide her complaint dated 05.10.2013.
As per complainant, she was married to Sh. Rohit Sharma S/o Sh. Ashok Sharma on 08.05.2009 as per Hindu Customs and Ceremonies.
Her parents had spent more than their financial capacity and gave household articles, gifts and cash amount which is still in possession of the accused persons and is being misused by them.
3) As per complainant, the husband of the complainant unfortunately died in a road accident on 09.12.2009.

It is stated that on 27.12.2009 her brother in law, sister in law (jethani) and sister in law (nanad) thrown her out of the matrimonial home in wearing clothes and left her at the house of her parents in Maujpur, Delhi.
Complainant also alleged that accused persons has refused to return her stridhan and dowry articles despite her repeated requests.

Digitally signed by SANJEEV JAIN SANJEEV Date:
 JAIN 2025.03.03
After investigation charge sheet was filed.
5) Vide impugned order dated 19.10.2024, Ld. JMFC directed to frame charges against accused persons under section 498A/406/34 IPC.
Charge under section 174A IPC was also framed against accused Meera.
6) Ld.
Counsel for revisionist submitted that his submissions has not been considered by the Ld.
Trial court and no reason has been recorded in order dated 19.10.2024 either to reject his arguments or to frame the charges against the accused persons/ revisionists.
It is submitted by ld.
Counsel that material on record has not been considered by the ld.

Trial court and therefore, the impugned order dated 19.10.2024 in respect of framing of charge against the revisionist under section 498A/34 IPC,
406/34 IPC may be set aside.
Charge under section 174A IPC against accused Meera has not been challenged and she is not a revisionist in this case.

sentences.text: 2 7) In a warrant trial case under Code of Criminal Procedure (in short CrPC), under section 239 CrPC accused may be discharged if the Magistrate considers the charge against the accused to be groundless, but he is required to record reasons.

Under section 240 CrPC if upon such consideration, examination and hearing, Magistrate is of the opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed the offence which such Magistrate is competent to try he may frame the charge.
Framing of charge is an important stage of a warrant trial case.

It is settled position of law that at the time of framing of charge court has to take a prima facie view of the material placed before Digitally signed by SANJEEV SANJEEV JAIN JAIN Date:
2025.03.03 16:24:49 +0530 the court and does not require to go into the roving inquiry in respect of the merits of the allegations/evidence.
Under section 239 or 240 CrPC at the time of discharge or framing of charges, Magistrate is required to consider the material on record and the submissions of prosecution and accused persons.
For framing of charge under section 240 CrPC Magistrate has to form an opinion that there is ground for presuming that accused has committed the offence.
The presumption required under section 240 CrPC cannot be drawn by the Magistrate subjectively but it must be based on the consideration of material on record.
Under section 240 CrPC consideration, examination if any, and hearing by the Magistrate are essential conditions.
The order of charge is not required to be very detailed like a judgement but it should reflect the reasoning, the grounds for presuming that accused has committed the offence.
Magistrate is required to give reasons for framing of charge after consideration of material on record.
In the absence of a reasoned order, it is difficult to assess what material had been considered by the ld. Trail court.
In my opinion, reasoned order under Section 239 CrPC or 240 CrPC is essential condition under the law.
8) Order dated 19.10.2024 clearly reflect that no reason whatsoever have been given by the ld.
Trial court for reaching on the conclusion for framing of charge against the accused persons/revisionist which is not sustainable in the eyes of the law.
Passing a non speaking order at the time of framing of charge substantially effects the rights of the accused persons.

9) Keeping in view the above discussion, in my opinion, order dated 19.10.2024 being a non speaking order suffers from SANJEEV Date:
 JAIN 2025.03.03  16:25:01  +0530 material illegality, therefore, the said order is set aside.
Ld. Trial court is directed to give an opportunity of hearing to the parties and to pass a reasoned order on the point of charge.
Revision petition is accordingly disposed of.
10) Trial court record be sent back to the ld.
Trial court alongwith copy of order for information and compliance.
All the revisionists are directed to appear before the ld.
Trial court on 10.03.2025 at 2.00 pm.
